newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Investors shun Ukraine 3-mth T-bill as yield jumps.
newsitem.headline: Investors shun Ukraine 3-mth T-bill as yield jumps.

text.p: Yields on Ukrainian three-month Treasury bills jumped on Tuesday as investors put off by a falling currency and recent drop in yields shunned the paper, traders said on Wednesday.
Three-month T-bill yields rose to 42.45 percent at the November 12 auction from 30.19 percent on October 29. Yields on six- and nine-month paper were little changed.
Ilya Rafalovsky of the First Ukrainian International Bank said yields of about 30 percent have caused investors to lose interest in buying short-term paper.
"Six-, nine- and twelve-month paper is far more interesting. A drop in interest in short-term paper has occurred along with the recent drop in yields," Rafalovsky said.
The hryvnia was unchanged at 1.870 on Wednesday on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange but has fallen steadily from 1.760 in early October.
Serhy Matveychuk of Perkombank said that the Finance Ministry was obliged to accept a rise in three-month yields because it feared it might not be able to meet repayments on earlier issues.
Traders said investors were buying dollars rather than domestic T-bills.
Matveychuk predicted yields could rise to 50 percent by the end of the year.
Finance Minister Vasyl Hureyev said last month that Ukraine would try to increase the quantity of longer-term T-bills it sells.
The next auction for three-, six-, nine- and 12-month bills is scheduled for November 14. --Aleksandras Budrys, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
